chapterName: Empire: The Fall of the West (AD 395-476)

briefing.title: The Roman Empire, AD 395
paragraphs: In January 395 the last emperor to rule the whole Roman world dies. His two young sons split it: one rules the East from Constantinople, the other the West, from Italy to Spain and Gaul. Neither has real talent, and rival ministers pull the strings.

Inside the borders live armed Goths, refugees from the Huns who crushed a Roman army at Adrianople. Over the next eighty years Goths, Vandals and Huns will test the West. Can its generals hold it together, or will Rome itself fall?

timelines.name: Milestones of the Fall
timelines.blurb: Four turning points from the Gothic victory to the last western emperor.

events.label: Goths destroy an eastern army
events.fact: At Adrianople, in modern European Turkey, the rebel Goths killed the eastern emperor himself.

events.label: Alaric's Goths sack Rome
events.fact: It was the first time in almost 800 years that Rome had fallen to a foreign enemy.

events.label: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
events.fact: Aetius's coalition fought Attila's Huns over a ridge until dark near Troyes.

events.label: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus
events.fact: By convention this marks the end of the Western Roman Empire.

timelines.name: Goths, Vandals and Huns
timelines.blurb: Six steps in the West's long unravelling.

events.label: Empire divided between two sons
events.fact: One son took the East from Constantinople, the other the West, and both became puppets of rival ministers.

events.label: Alaric invades Italy
events.fact: The frightened court soon moved its capital from Milan to marsh-shielded Ravenna.

events.label: Half-Vandal general executed
events.fact: Accused of treason, he was lured out of a church sanctuary and killed, and thousands of barbarian troops fled to Alaric.

events.label: Visigoths given land in Aquitaine
events.fact: A whole people now lived inside the empire under its own king and army, only loosely obeying Rome.

events.label: Vandals capture Carthage
events.fact: Rome lost rich Africa, its main source of grain, to an independent Vandal kingdom with a powerful navy.

events.label: Vandals plunder Rome
events.fact: For two weeks they looted the city, far more thoroughly than the Goths had in 410.

timelines.name: From Refugees to Historians
timelines.blurb: Eight events, from the Gothic crossing to the first great history of the fall.

events.label: Goths settle inside the empire
events.fact: Fleeing the Huns, nomadic horsemen of the steppe, huge numbers of Goths entered Roman territory.

events.label: Draw against Alaric at Pollentia
events.fact: The half-Vandal general fought Alaric to a draw, then beat him at Verona.

events.label: Alaric sets up a puppet emperor
events.fact: During his second siege of Rome Alaric made his own emperor, then deposed him a few months later.

events.label: Attila unites the Huns
events.fact: Attila ruled many Germanic peoples and squeezed vast sums of gold out of the eastern empire.

events.label: Attila razes Aquileia
events.fact: Disease, hunger and perhaps an embassy led by the pope then persuaded him to leave Italy.

events.label: A capable emperor is executed
events.fact: He had rebuilt the army to retake Africa, but traitors burned his fleet and his own general had him killed.

events.label: Last Roman enclave in Gaul ends
events.fact: A Roman enclave in northern Gaul outlasted the conventional end of the West by ten years.

events.label: Decline and Fall begins to appear
events.fact: Its English author blamed barbarians, Christians and the Romans' own quarrels.

trueFalseDecks.name: The Gothic Crisis (395-410)
trueFalseDecks.blurb: From the divided empire to Alaric's sack of Rome.

cards.claim: The Goths entered the empire because they were fleeing the Huns.
cards.why: From 376 huge numbers of Goths, fleeing the nomadic Huns, lived inside the empire.

cards.claim: At Adrianople in 378 the Goths killed the western emperor.
cards.why: They destroyed an eastern army and killed the eastern emperor.

cards.claim: The frightened western court moved its capital from Milan to Ravenna.
cards.why: Ravenna, near the Adriatic, was shielded by marshes and had an escape route by sea.

cards.claim: Alaric decisively defeated the half-Vandal general at Pollentia in 402.
cards.why: Pollentia was a draw, and the general then beat Alaric at Verona.

cards.claim: In 408 Rome paid Alaric about 1,650 kg (5,000 pounds) of gold.
cards.why: It also paid nearly 10 tonnes (30,000 pounds) of silver, melting down pagan statues to make up the sum.

cards.claim: Alaric's real demand was to be made emperor himself.
cards.why: His real demands were modest: land and grain for his people, which the emperor refused.

cards.claim: The Goths entered Rome through the Salarian Gate on 24 August 410.
cards.why: Some said traitors had opened the gate, others that hunger had.

cards.claim: The Goths' sack of 410 included a general massacre of the citizens.
cards.why: By the standards of the age it was restrained: no general massacre, and the two great basilicas served as sanctuaries.

trueFalseDecks.name: Huns, Vandals and the End (410-476)
trueFalseDecks.blurb: From the debate over the sack to the last emperor.

cards.claim: The bishop who wrote The City of God argued that Christians' real home was a heavenly city.
cards.why: He rejected the idea that true religion should bring worldly success; no earthly disaster could touch that heavenly city.

cards.claim: The taxes lost with Africa could have paid for nearly 4,000 infantry.
cards.why: They could have paid for nearly 40,000 infantry.

cards.claim: The emperor's sister sent Attila her ring and a plea for help.
cards.why: Trapped in an engagement she hated, she gave Attila his excuse to claim half the western empire as dowry.

cards.claim: Attila was killed in the battle on the Catalaunian Plains.
cards.why: It was the Visigothic king who was killed; Attila withdrew to his wagon camp and died suddenly in 453.

cards.claim: In 454 the western emperor stabbed Aetius to death with his own hands.
cards.why: A year later Aetius's supporters murdered the emperor in revenge.

cards.claim: The Vandals plundered Rome in 455 less thoroughly than the Goths had in 410.
cards.why: They plundered it for two weeks, far more thoroughly, and left with huge treasure and an imperial princess.

cards.claim: Odoacer gave Romulus Augustulus a yearly pension of 6,000 gold coins (solidi).
cards.why: Said to have pitied the 16-year-old, he spared him and sent him to relatives in Campania.

cards.claim: The East survived partly because it had a longer river frontier to guard than the West.
cards.why: The West had some 2,000 km of Rhine and Danube frontier; the East's heartland was shielded by Constantinople's walls and the sea.

oddOneOut.why: Alaric blockaded Rome, made a puppet emperor and asked for land and grain. It was the frightened imperial court that moved to Ravenna.

items: Fires near the old Senate house
oddOneOut.why: The first three happened in the Gothic sack of 410. The imperial princess was carried off by the Vandals in 455.
Three events belong to the year 410. The Visigoths were given land in Aquitaine in 418.
Visigoths, Franks and Burgundians joined Aetius's coalition against Attila. The Vandals were by then ruling their own kingdom from Carthage.

items: An embassy led by the pope
oddOneOut.why: Disease, hunger and perhaps a papal embassy turned Attila back from Italy in 452. No battle with Aetius is described that year.

items: God's punishment of a proud city
oddOneOut.why: Modern historians point to plague, climate and taxes. God's punishment was a Christian explanation offered after the sack of 410.

whoAmI.name: Barbarian Leaders
whoAmI.blurb: Kings and officers who shook the Western Empire.

people.name: Alaric
clues: I revolted in 395 after being denied high Roman command.
Twice I was cornered in Greece, and twice I was allowed to escape.
When senators boasted, I laughed that the thickest grass is easier to cut than the thinnest.
In 410 I led the Goths into Rome through the Salarian Gate.

people.name: Attila
clues: From 444 I squeezed vast sums of gold out of the eastern empire.
An emperor's sister sent me her ring, and I claimed half the West as her dowry.
In 452 I razed Aquileia, but disease and hunger turned me back.
As king of the Huns I fought Aetius on the Catalaunian Plains.

people.name: Odoacer
clues: I led mercenaries who rebelled when their promised land never came.
I sent the imperial regalia to the emperor in Constantinople.
I spared a 16-year-old and gave him 6,000 gold coins a year.
On 4 September 476 I forced the last western emperor off his throne.

whoAmI.name: Romans of the Falling West
whoAmI.blurb: Generals and an emperor of the western court.

people.name: The half-Vandal general
clues: Historians still argue why I twice let my enemy escape in Greece.
I fought Alaric to a draw at Pollentia, then beat him at Verona.
I was commander-in-chief of the West and guardian to the boy emperor.
Accused of treason, I was lured out of a church and executed in 408.
reviewFlags: "The half-Vandal general" appears fewer than 2 times in the chapter

people.name: Aetius
clues: I often fought Goths, Franks and rebels with Hunnic mercenaries.
I united Visigoths, Alans, Franks and Burgundians, old enemies, in one coalition.
In 454 the emperor stabbed me to death with his own hands.
For two decades I held the West together and stood against Attila in 451.

people.name: Romulus Augustulus
clues: I was never recognised as emperor outside Italy.
My father, once Attila's secretary, crowned me in 475.
My name honoured Rome's founder and its first emperor, but rivals mocked it as 'little Augustus'.
Deposed at 16, I was sent to live with relatives in Campania.

places.name: Constantinople
places.why: The great city on the Bosphorus from which the eastern half of the empire was governed.

places.name: Adrianople
places.why: Here on 9 August 378 the Goths destroyed an eastern army and killed its emperor.

places.name: Ravenna
places.why: Shielded by marshes with an escape route by sea, it replaced Milan as the western capital.

places.name: Carthage
places.why: Captured by the Vandals in 439, it became the capital of their independent kingdom with a powerful navy.

places.name: Orléans
places.why: Its Alan defenders held out against Attila's siege, which many historians see as the real turning point of 451.

places.name: Catalaunian Plains
places.why: Near Troyes, Aetius's coalition fought Attila's Huns around 20 June 451.
places.coordinates: Wikipedia: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains

places.name: Aquileia
places.why: This city at the head of the Adriatic was razed by Attila when he invaded Italy in 452.
